about: Phase 8 (scheduleVersion 3) adds acts-v3h and acts-v3t: encounter pool sets, the provenance-mix draw, anomaly nodes and the finale act. acts-v1, acts-v2 and act1 ship unchanged and keep stamp 2 ("version"), so a run saved on them loads and replays as before. The close-out (family 25) enabled both finales (acts-v3h: the Heist finale, acts-v3t: Tekahn with the hero relay) and made them the defaults: a new run rolls one of "defaults" from its seed, never one whose finale fixes a boss row its hero row excludes (DALA_Tekahn always follows acts-v3h); "default" names the first for tools that read one schedule. Step 9 (scheduleVersion 4) adds acts-v4h and acts-v4t at stamp 4 ("version": 4): v3's node shape and acts, with the step-9 tuning keys (draw provenance-mix-v2 and its drawTuning, upgradeEveryFloors, per-act treasureRarity and bundleAfterTreasure, the chapter twist pools, per-fight finale curves, the Tekahn finale's turnCap and formRatchet) that only a stamp-4 run reads (DungeonRun.Tuned); acts-v3h and acts-v3t keep stamp 3 ("version": 3), so every released run plays as released. The values are uncalibrated initial values (handoff/phase9/values.md). Step 9 makes acts-v4h and acts-v4t the defaults ("default" names acts-v4h): a new run rolls one of them as it rolled the v3 pair; a run saved on acts-v3h or acts-v3t keeps its schedule and stamp. "defaultWithoutEncounters" is what a data set loaded without encounters-v1.json follows (tools and suites that load the pre-phase-8 files; never the shipped mode).

rules.reason: final (step 9, lane R recheck): its Treasures are the Dalaran Heist active treasures (hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Anomaly_-_Glittering: "This anomaly generates The Dalaran Heist treasures"), which are run rewards admitted for the run player's run deck only: no generation pool and no boss may hold one (DungeonRunAdmission.RunTreasureLift), and several write run state (DALA_718, DALA_719, DALA_721). Step 9 shares treasures player-side only (plan D6) and gives no boss a treasure, so a rule for both players stays out of scope; the rule stays rejected
